notes: Rear-panel I/O and labels were read directly off the official Telos Alliance Omnia.9 Quick-Start Installation Guide's rear-panel photo (Main Analog I/O, Main Digital I/O, Aux Digital I/O, Composite I/O blocks) plus the guide's network-port diagram; cross-checked against the manufacturer product page (telosalliance.com/radio-processing/radio-processors/omnia9). All AES/EBU digital audio jacks are physically female XLR3 connectors carrying an AES3 signal, coded here as "aes3". Composite I/O BNCs carry analog MPX/composite signal, not SDI, so no SDI grade applies. AoIP (dual RJ45: AES67/Livewire+ + WAN) is standard on units built since April 2018; legacy pre-2018 units instead have single ports labeled "Ethernet" and "Future" and need an MKII upgrade for AES67/Livewire+ I/O — treat this device as the current MKII-era rear panel. eth-1g grade on the two RJ45 ports is inferred from the product page's statement of "100 and 1000BASE-T" Ethernet support (the quick-start guide itself does not print a speed grade next to the ports), so treat as medium-confidence for that specific attribute. The front-panel headphone jack's connector size (assumed 6.35mm/1/4" TRS, industry-standard for this class of broadcast processor) and the front-panel USB port's exact type/version (assumed USB-A; version unstated in the sourced documents) are inferred, not explicitly confirmed in the sourced material. Power: dual redundant, hot-swappable internal supplies, 100-264VAC 47-63Hz autosensing, each with a standard IEC power-cord inlet (referred to in Telos's troubleshooting FAQ as "IEC male connectors"); modeled here as two "iec" ports since the exact C13/C14 vs C7/C19 variant is not spelled out.
